The Meta Enterprise Platform will focus on turning the company's AI stack into products and services that companies can deploy for their own businesses. MongoDB has appointed Dev Ittycheria as interim chief executive while the board searches for a permanent replacement.

articles.headline: OpenAI Scraps Release of New AI Model Over Safety Concerns
articles.blurb: OpenAI is scrapping the release of GPT-6.1 Astra due to safety concerns. The company had aimed to launch the model in October, but the model performed poorly on tests measuring alignment compared to its predecessor. GPT-6.1 Astra showed higher levels of deception, and it would push ahead on tasks without asking users for permission. It would also reach for external tools and services even if it might be unsafe. OpenAI says it is working to investigate a range of agent security incidents and address the safety issues underneath them.

articles.headline: Airbound: As We May Move
articles.blurb: Airbound's first drone, the TRT, weighs in at 1.5 kilograms. The eVTOL can carry a 1-kilogram payload and can land and launch from anywhere, making logistics possible where infrastructure doesn't exist. The company's goal is to move mass more cheaply than anyone else. Its main focus is cost per kilogram-kilometer, and everything is secondary to that.

articles.headline: SpaceX's Starship Makes It to Orbit for the First Time, but Returns to Earth Early
articles.blurb: SpaceX's Starship circled Earth on Monday. The spacecraft had to return to Earth after less than two orbits instead of the planned six because of engine problems that occurred during liftoff. The Starship spacecraft splashed down with a fiery explosion in the North Pacific near Hawaii before noon. Reaching orbit is a key milestone towards SpaceX's goal of eventually sending people to Mars as well as NASA's plans to send astronauts back to the moon.

articles.headline: The Code Nobody Reads
articles.blurb: Know what's worth reading, and on the code you don't read, build checks you actually trust. Good code is a love letter to the next developer. The next developer is now an agent, so the letter looks different now. You need to pass on code that agents can change without breaking something it can't see. The craft has now moved to the parts that decide whether the code deserves to be trusted.

articles.headline: Anthropic has launched Claude Sonnet 5.5
articles.blurb: Claude Sonnet 5.5 scores just 2 points behind Opus 5.5 (max) on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. However, it uses around 60% more tokens to reach that performance. The model is priced at $2/$10 per million tokens of input/output, matching GPT-6 Sol. Sonnet 5.5 still lags on factual knowledge as it is a smaller class model than Opus 5.5, but it has a lower hallucination rate.

articles.headline: Apps, Agents, and Aggregation
articles.blurb: The new prize in technology is to be the only interface users need for everything, with agents using computers on users' behalf and generating whatever UI is needed. For people who are using agents, this is obvious. Apps are just a vehicle for people to accomplish something or entertain themselves. Once people can get straight to the job to be done, it will seem odd that they did it any other way.

It has a well-established track record of being able to find the simple, obvious-in-hindsight breakthroughs that unlock new kinds of consumption behavior. This, along with its durable distribution strategy, will help it become the winner in the AI race.

Around $5 trillion worth of businesses in the US will change hands by 2035. Most of these belong to boomers heading into retirement. Many of them have nobody lined up to buy them. This guide walks readers through how to find the right business, buy it, and run it with agents.

articles.headline: The Rise Of The Neo Neo Lab
articles.blurb: The last generation of enterprise software was built around proprietary data and workflows. The next will be built around the intelligence derived from them. Frontier labs will continue pushing the ceiling of general intelligence, but enterprises will take that intelligence and teach it what only they know. Companies with enough proprietary data, expert judgment, workflow volume, and distribution will have the raw materials to produce proprietary intelligence of their own.

articles.blurb: Pat Grady frames AI as a technology wave that is bigger, faster, and fundamentally different because progress increasingly comes from computation. His reflection for Boston College's Investment Committee examines how that shift is reshaping technology and investing.

articles.headline: The Irreplaceables. The Employees to Never Let Go. Even If You Have to Invent a Role
articles.blurb: You will always regret letting one of the truly irreplaceable people on your team leave. This usually happens with scale. As things change, you need larger teams and different processes, and new executives may not think these employees are so irreplaceable. However, they are the ones who truly know how and why everything works and are often the best to help figure out how the next move can work. Top performers are the people you'd rehire into their role - irreplaceables are the ones you would rehire into a role that doesn't exist yet.

articles.headline: Gusto's Cofounder Says AI Made Your Revenue Worth Less to an Acquirer and Your Speed Worth More
articles.blurb: An acquirer may love your product and still decide it's faster to build its own. Gusto's cofounder explains that AI has shortened the time the company expects internal development to take, making acquisitions harder to justify. His example is hypothetical. If buying a company saves 18 months' worth of $50 million to Gusto, a business with $5 million in revenue might fit at a 10x multiple. One with $50 million in revenue probably won't. Your revenue can raise your asking price without increasing how much development time the buyer saves.

articles.headline: Alexandria (Website)
articles.blurb: Alexandria is a knowledge library for superintelligence that gives agents tools like the live web, official providers, and specialized indexes. It provides a world of data with just one library. There are over 113 million indexed sources, 93 providers, 640 capabilities, and 20 categories. Data providers can join a waitlist to get paid for sharing their data.

articles.headline: Parallel (Website)
articles.blurb: Parallel provides data connectors that connect agents to sources beyond the public web. Categories span company, people, financial, commerce, web, news, and health care & life sciences data. Visitors can request a source or connect their data to the platform. Pricing is pay-as-you-go, and users can run up to 5,000 requests per month for free.

articles.headline: Introducing n8n Agents
articles.blurb: n8n now has Agents. Developers describe what an agent should do, give it a model, tools, and workflows, and it works out the steps itself. An agent can be reached through Slack, run on a schedule, or called from any workflow. The same agent runs in every one of those places. Videos on how to use the agents in real-world applications are available.

articles.headline: Value Accrual Flywheel
articles.blurb: Software accrues value by creating dependencies that compound over time and raise switching costs. These dependencies compound internally as the product embeds deeper into workflows and externally through network effects and ecosystem adoption. Dependencies inside critical systems get a value multiplier because ripping them out threatens the business itself. Resulting revenue from these embedded software systems funds new features that create new dependencies, creating a Value Accrual Flywheel.

articles.headline: The Cautious Tale Of Cal AI
articles.blurb: Before Cal AI reached a reported $50 million in annual recurring revenue, one founder's mom had to co-sign the company bank account. Two of the four founders were still in high school. People now ask how they assembled that team, but the answer involves a cousin's YouTube recommendation, a cold DM, and meeting a future cofounder while working at another startup. There was no recruiting process to copy. The advice is more realistic: look for someone who is available and can learn, and expect to offer enough money or equity to make joining worthwhile.

It offers natural language querying, automatic dependency mapping, and a dedicated agent observability workflow spanning frameworks like LangGraph, CrewAI, and the Vercel AI SDK.

articles.blurb: Alibaba has open-sourced OpenCodeReview, an Apache-2.0 code review tool that combines deterministic file and rule matching with AI analysis to flag issues like null pointers and SQL injection. It matches Claude Code's precision using roughly one-ninth the tokens in tests, though outside reviewers found recall as low as 20 percent.

articles.headline: Trading a Cloud Identity for Your Own: Workload Attestation on Managed Compute
articles.blurb: Netflix engineers developed a method to bridge AWS IAM roles with internal identities for Apache Spark workloads on Amazon EMR. The system maps each Data Project identity to a dedicated IAM role, allowing a control plane to sign metadata that an identity service verifies against a cloud proof of possession. This approach ensures that workloads running on managed compute obtain valid certificates from the internal PKI, called Metatron, without relying on the workload's own account of itself.

articles.headline: A Type Stronger than the Sum of its Components
articles.blurb: Rust APIs can encode stronger invariants by turning individual enum variants into dedicated types instead of accepting broader string or path values. Wrapping std::path::Component variants in types such as NormalComponent and ParentDirComponent lets the compiler enforce properties like safe path joins and prevents callers from passing values containing .., absolute paths, or other invalid components.

articles.headline: Improving site performance by shipping more CSS
articles.blurb: GitHub migrated github.com from CSS-in-JS to CSS Modules to remove client- and server-side styling overhead at scale. The migration cut Primer server-side rendering time by 55%, reduced component initialization time by 25%, and later improved SSR by up to 22% on some pages while thousands of sx usages were gradually replaced through feature flags, visual regression tests, codemods, and staged rollouts.

articles.headline: scriptc (GitHub Repo)
articles.blurb: scriptc compiles TypeScript and JavaScript to native executables, WebAssembly modules, and other outputs including C and LLVM IR. It uses the TypeScript compiler for parsing and type checking, and static builds include a small native runtime without a JavaScript engine.

articles.headline: Openrig (GitHub Repo)
articles.blurb: OpenRig is a multi-agent harness that manages Claude Code and Codex as a unified team within tmux sessions. It defines agent teams in YAML and includes starter configurations like a four-seat conveyor, a product-team with seven seats, and a secrets-manager example that runs a HashiCorp Vault instance. The tool requires Node.js and integrates a local daemon, CLI, terminal UI, and MCP server. Users should read the documentation about system changes before installing, as OpenRig writes hooks, trust settings, and provider integrations during setup.

articles.headline: Maximizing Apache Spark availability: Mitigating compute stockouts with flexible VMs and other best practices
articles.blurb: Google's Managed Service for Apache Spark now supports flexible VMs, letting clusters rank multiple acceptable machine families and storage types so provisioning automatically falls back during regional capacity stockouts rather than failing. Google recommends pairing ranked configurations with AutoZone routing, autoscaling, and regional fallbacks for resilience.

articles.headline: How Cloudflare addressed a cross-tenant data exposure vulnerability in Containers
articles.blurb: Security researcher Oren Yomtov reported a vulnerability in Cloudflare Containers that allowed residual data recovery from storage blocks used by other customers on the same host. The issue stemmed from a configuration setting that skipped zeroing newly allocated blocks, potentially exposing directory structures, database pages, and application data. Cloudflare has remediated the vulnerability across its fleet and found no evidence of malicious exploitation.

articles.headline: Bun Rewrites 535K Lines of Zig into Rust in Four Months, Eliminates Numerous Memory Leaks

articles.headline: Artists, Game Designers and Producers Hit Hard as Microsoft Cuts 277 Jobs in Washington State
articles.blurb: Microsoft cut 277 jobs in the Seattle region, according to a newly public WARN Act filing, with artists, game designers and producers among the hardest hit. Art, production, design, and audio roles total 77 positions, while software engineering is the largest single category at 60. Of the cuts, 252 were at the Redmond campus, and 25 were remote, part of a wider Xbox restructuring that also moves the next Halo game to Activision.

articles.headline: YouTube Releases New AI Features for Creators within its Studio App
articles.blurb: YouTube is adding AI tools to its Studio app that critique unpublished videos on pacing, structure, and storytelling before creators publish. A new research feed shows what content performs well on the platform, and thumbnails and titles can be generated to match a creator's own style. Creators have already run over 40 million title and thumbnail A/B tests, and Studio will soon test three video cuts and swap out weak thumbnails automatically.

articles.headline: Apple's XR headset plans are supposedly on life support, as it experiments with new design ideas
articles.blurb: Apple is exploring a completely redesigned Vision headset that could address the Vision Pro's biggest weakness—its weight—using lighter materials or moving the processor and battery into a separate puck similar to Meta's new VR glasses. Several concepts are reportedly under consideration, but development remains uncertain, and any new headset is unlikely to arrive before 2028 or 2029.

articles.headline: The 5 Big Lessons Designers Must Learn
articles.blurb: Five lessons run through design work: someone always has to pay for an idea, and framing it as higher quality sells better than calling it good design. Power, not talent, decides most projects, since whoever controls budget, schedule, and goals is the real designer, leaving others to work through influence instead. What counts as good depends on context, such as affordability and bureaucracy, and products bought before they're used are often designed to sell rather than to serve.

articles.headline: Google has the best AI money can buy. Its products still feel broken
articles.blurb: Google's AI-powered search is eroding trust not because Gemini is inherently incapable, but because probabilistic answers have been inserted into an interface that users expect to deliver deterministic, verifiable results without clearly communicating uncertainty. The deeper problem may be organizational: weak feedback loops between product teams and real users can produce fragmented features optimized for internal goals rather than actual workflows. For teams integrating AI, the key is to distinguish surfaces where occasional mistakes are acceptable from those where accuracy is fundamental, while preserving direct user feedback and making uncertainty visible.

articles.headline: How to Sync a Design System with Claude Design
articles.blurb: Syncing a design system with Claude Design creates a mirror: a compiled, self-rendering copy of the component library, so Claude designs with the real components. The sync runs with /design-sync from Claude Code and checks and fixes its own work before uploading, and the mirror is a one-way snapshot. With shadcn and Tailwind v4, the key steps are an entry file with type definitions, a compiled stylesheet with safelisted layout utilities, fonts listed in extraFonts, and a conventions file. Storybook is optional, but it provides the reference that makes the sync verifiable.

articles.headline: MOKSi gives GiftTrees the confidence to be both good and profitable
articles.blurb: GiftTrees worked with MOKSi to reposition itself as a profitable business that creates positive environmental and social impact, centered on the proposition “impact made easy” and an intentionally upbeat, anti-guilt tone. The refreshed identity combines a leaf-and-bow logo, expressive typography, green with vibrant purple, orange, and red, and positive imagery to distinguish the company from traditional charity and sustainability branding. The result gives GiftTrees a clearer way to unite people, planet, and profit while supporting its ambition to scale from more than five million trees planted toward one billion.

articles.headline: When Chat is the Wrong UI
articles.blurb: Chat has stayed the default way to work with AI for three years, but it suits people who don't know what they want, not those who do. In the GitHub Copilot app, a canvas is a small full-stack application, with no browser chrome, that talks back and forth with the agent. Examples include a playable Connect 4 game, a local package manager, and a workflow tool that automates research and planning so a developer can step back.

articles.headline: Inca Kola rebrands as the world's other cola war heats up
articles.blurb: Inca Kola simplified its identity in 2016 by removing elements such as Peru's silhouette and its founding date, creating a cleaner, more modern logo but prompting criticism that the brand is losing some of its distinctly Peruvian character. Rather than relying on explicit national symbols, the new system emphasizes belonging through imagery of social gatherings and food, while turning the logo's distinctive shape into a flexible framing device. The identity also expands into sound with a four-note mnemonic created from traditional glass cola bottles, reinforcing familiar brand associations while modernizing the overall experience.

articles.headline: Easter Eggs in Product Design & Web Design
articles.blurb: Hidden features and secret interactions make a product feel delightful and memorable, tapping into the dopamine hit of discovering something unexpected.

articles.headline: The Death of Web Development Education
articles.blurb: Generative AI has gutted the market for web-development education.

articles.headline: Revolut trials Pay with Smile
articles.blurb: Revolut customers can now pay for coffee with their face at three Kiss the Hippo cafés in Bloomsbury, Chelsea, and Soho. The in-store facial recognition checkout, Revolut Pay with Smile, allows customers to pay for their purchases with a simple glance, with 0% processing fees for merchants on all transactions.

articles.headline: Monzo in talks about multibillion-pound sale to Brazil's Nubank
articles.blurb: Monzo is in early talks with Nubank parent Nu Holdings about a potential £8 billion to £10 billion sale, with Morgan Stanley and Qatalyst advising as Monzo also weighs a new funding round to support European expansion. A deal would give Nubank an immediate UK and European banking foothold through Monzo's 16 million customers and £1.7 billion of annual revenue, while likely ending Monzo's near-term path to a standalone IPO.

articles.headline: ACH use rises for B2B payments
articles.blurb: ACH has overtaken checks as the most common US B2B payment method by transaction count, rising from 25% of payments in 2015 to 41% in 2024 while checks fell from 32% to 13%. ACH transaction value nearly doubled to $70 trillion over the period, though wires still dominate by value at roughly $1 quadrillion, showing that businesses are steadily shifting routine payments toward electronic rails even as checks remain widely used.

articles.headline: Agent Wars: Amazon vs. Muse
articles.blurb: Simon Taylor argues that Amazon's decision to block Meta's Muse agent is an early battle over who owns the customer, captures commerce fees, and bears liability when AI agents transact on users' behalf. He expects the key infrastructure layer to be “Know Your Agent” standards that authenticate agents, define delegated authority, and allocate liability, with merchants, wallets, card networks, platforms, and infrastructure providers all competing to control that trust layer.

articles.headline: UK banks pilot tokenised deposit transactions
articles.blurb: UK banks have collaborated to complete the first live customer transactions using tokenised sterling deposits. The transactions were delivered through the Great British Tokenised Deposit (GBTD) initiative, which was convened by UK Finance and involves Barclays, HSBC UK, Lloyds Banking Group, Monzo, Nationwide, NatWest, and Santander.

articles.headline: Cleverbridge completes France's first Passkey-authenticated agentic purchase, on a Revolut card
articles.blurb: Cleverbridge, a managed global commerce platform for software and technology companies, today announced that it completed France's first Passkey-authenticated agentic payment in a live checkout in a pilot with Visa and Revolut announced earlier this month.

articles.headline: Numeral raises $100M Series C to expand AI-powered tax compliance
articles.blurb: Numeral raised a $100 million Series C led by Insight Partners, bringing total funding to $157 million as it expands its AI-powered sales tax compliance platform across software, manufacturing, distribution, and wholesale. The company says transaction volume is up 327% year over year and is positioning itself as end-to-end tax infrastructure spanning nexus monitoring, registrations, calculation, filings, remittance, and exemption certificates, with support for VAT and GST in more than 90 countries.

articles.headline: SEC clarifies that certain staked Ethereum receipt tokens are not securities
articles.blurb: SEC staff clarified that liquid-staking receipt tokens tied to non-security crypto assets like ETH generally are not securities when they simply represent ownership of the underlying staked asset and do not add separate rights, returns, or managerial promises. The guidance builds on the SEC's earlier position on liquid staking, but remains staff guidance rather than binding law, meaning its treatment could change through future rulemaking, legislation, or a different administration.

articles.headline: Tools Are Getting Better. Are We?
articles.blurb: Product work creates both output and learning, and AI risks accelerating the first without compounding the second.

articles.headline: Ramp turns bill pay into a one-night Broadway musical
articles.blurb: Ramp is staging Bill Pay The Musical for one night on Broadway on September 25, starring Billy Porter, Billy Zane, and Jessica Vosk as an elaborate promotion for its accounts payable product.

articles.headline: BNPL regulation: the growing role of data in credit decisioning
articles.blurb: The old BNPL model made borrowing feel like a payment choice rather than a credit decision.

articles.headline: CISA Says Attackers Are Exploiting Two Critical Citrix NetScaler Flaws Globally
articles.blurb: CISA added CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 to its KEV catalog after confirming global exploitation. Both have CVSS scores of 9.5. The flaws enable unauthenticated command execution, remote code execution, or denial of service. CVE-2026-88772 requires DTLS, which VPN virtual servers enable by default. Administrators should patch, inspect for compromise, isolate affected appliances, revoke access, rotate secrets, and investigate connected systems.

articles.headline: BOK Faces Scrutiny Over Cybersecurity After Staff Data Breach
articles.blurb: The Bank of Korea (BOK) is facing scrutiny over its cybersecurity program following a data breach earlier this year. The breach occurred in May and June after attackers accessed a GitHub system used by a contractor for an online training program. The exposed data included employees' names, email addresses, phone numbers, positions, duties, and passwords for 186 employees.

articles.headline: Elementor WordPress Flaw Lets Attackers Create Admin Accounts
articles.blurb: Security firm Patchstack warns users of the Elementor Website Builder plugin for WordPress about a new CSRF vulnerability that could allow unauthenticated attackers to create admin accounts. The vulnerability is a one-click attack that requires an authenticated admin to click a link that sends a malicious REST API request to create the account.

articles.headline: Containers Are No Longer a Security Boundary
articles.blurb: The traditional view of containers as a strong security and isolation mechanism is being eroded by the plethora of kernel vulnerabilities being uncovered. This article explains how a recent vulnerability in the AF_UNIX subsystem can be leveraged by attackers for container escapes. The authors recommend moving untrusted workloads to MicroVMs like Firecracker or Kata Containers for untrusted workloads.

articles.headline: From Exposure to Lockdown: How AWS Neutralizes Compromised IAM Credentials through Managed Policies
articles.blurb: AWS automatically attaches the AWSCompromisedKeyQuarantineV3 managed policy to an exposed IAM user within 10 seconds of a public GitHub push, with the CloudTrail AttachUserPolicy event misleadingly attributed to the victim's IAM user rather than to AWS automation. Each policy version tracked real-world attack evolution, with permissions added to block Lambda-based cryptomining, S3 data deletion for extortion, and Bedrock API abuse after Permiso's research exposed unauthorized InvokeModel calls. Security teams should alert on unexpected AttachUserPolicy events in CloudTrail, treat the quarantine event as confirmation of active key exposure rather than as resolution, and rotate all affected credentials before removing the policy.

articles.headline: PolinRider is A/B Testing its Way Past Your Detections
articles.blurb: DPRK's PolinRider malware spread through GitHub organizations by force-pushing rewritten commits from infected developers' machines, planting VS Code folderOpen tasks that run an obfuscated JavaScript payload disguised as fa-solid-400/500/900.woff2 and, since September 28, fa-solid-300.llf. OpenSourceMalware traced 853 force-pushes across three Binary-Mindz repos and found variants with different paths, obfuscators, and C2-reported build markers running in parallel, which it reads as deliberate A/B testing, while copied author dates and reused commit messages quietly reverted three cleanup attempts. Defenders should flag fake fonts by file content rather than name, scan every branch through bare clones, audit force-push activity logs, and enforce force-push blocking and signed commits on all branches.

articles.headline: tturl (GitHub Repo)
articles.blurb: tturl is an HTTP/2 CLI for finding tiny timing differences by releasing batches of requests and recording response arrival order, then either showing what happened or helping to distinguish a repeatable arrival-order signal from noise.

articles.headline: Kontext Security (Product Launch)
articles.blurb: Kontext Security runs a runtime enforcement platform that sits between AI agents and the systems they access. It checks each agent's identity, task, target resource, and requested action in real time. Teams can start in observe mode, then switch to enforcement to block unauthorized actions, as the platform logs every agent action and the decisions made, with context.

articles.headline: Google to critical infra orgs: Our AI scanners won't be evil, promise
articles.blurb: Google and Wiz launched Scan for Good using Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber and Red Agent with authorized scans targeting public websites, APIs, and applications, while human researchers validate findings and handle disclosure. Red Agent found a GitHub Actions injection flaw in Snowflake's connector, allowing command execution. Other cases exposed 8.8 million files, hospital systems, elderly residents' data, and railway administrator sessions.

articles.headline: House of Apple 2 on modern glibc
articles.blurb: This walkthrough breaks down House of Apple 2, a glibc FSOP technique that bypasses the vtable validation added in newer glibc. It points a FILE structure's vtable to legitimate wide-character stream code, which then dispatches to a second vtable that glibc does not range-check. Step by step in GDB, the author turns that unchecked indirect call into an arbitrary call, pivots the stack, and runs a ROP chain to a shell. The technique still works cleanly on glibc 2.43 (Ubuntu 26.04 and Fedora 44). Exact offsets and gadgets vary between builds, but the underlying control-flow trick remains the same.

articles.headline: Sender spoofing in Proton Mail via display-name homograph
articles.blurb: Proton Mail's web interface can show a forged sender that looks identical to a real one. The attacker sets a display name containing an address-shaped string like sundar@gmaiI[.]com where the capital I matches lowercase l in the default UI font. Messages from domains without DMARC arrive in the inbox with no authentication banner, even when SPF fails. A Reply-To header can route responses to an attacker's address without showing it unless the user expands headers, and the spoofed sender also appears unchanged in macOS desktop notifications, outside the app interface. The issue was reported in February 2025, confirmed and bounty-awarded in April 2025, and can still be reproduced as of September 2026.

articles.headline: Former US soldier gets nearly six-year sentence for hacking, extorting telecoms
articles.blurb: Former Army soldier Cameron Wagenius received 70 months in prison and nearly $295,000 in restitution.

articles.headline: DC Health Agency Exposes 400,000 Beneficiary Records
articles.blurb: The District of Columbia's health agency exposed data linked to 399,086 Medicaid and DC Healthcare Alliance beneficiaries.

articles.headline: Over 16,000 Supabase databases expose PII, passwords, auth tokens
articles.blurb: UpGuard identified more than 16,000 Supabase databases exposing readable tables. Analysis of their schemas indicated that more than half could expose personal information, with smaller subsets potentially exposing passwords or authentication tokens. The issue is misconfigured access controls rather than a newly discovered platform vulnerability, reinforcing the need for database authorization, exposure testing, and clear ownership of internally built tools.

articles.headline: Microsoft pauses KB5002907 update after Office license deactivations
articles.blurb: Microsoft has paused optional update KB5002907 after reports that it left some Office 2016 and 2019 installations unlicensed or, rarely, removed. Its recovery guidance is to reactivate or reinstall the affected product. Importantly, the update makes no changes where Microsoft 365 Apps updates are managed through Group Policy or Cloud Update. Support teams should check update history before treating unexpected licensing tickets as subscription or account problems.

articles.headline: 7 reasons IT managers fail to exceed your expectations
articles.blurb: Promoting a strong technologist does not automatically prepare them to manage people, business relationships, or competing operational priorities. This piece examines unclear expectations, insufficient leadership development, and the tendency to reward technical output without developing management skills. It is a useful operating-model check for CIOs overseeing support, infrastructure, SaaS, and business systems: define what managers own, coach them on business outcomes, and provide advancement paths for specialists who should remain individual contributors.

articles.headline: The SaaSpocalypse that wasn't, with Atlassian CEO Mike Cannon-Brookes
articles.blurb: In this Decoder interview, Mike Cannon-Brookes explains why Atlassian combined internal IT and AI enablement under its people leadership: employee adoption and changes to business systems are tightly connected. He also argues that AI will change SaaS workflows without eliminating the need for structured systems and human judgment. For CIOs, the interesting question is who owns the combined work of employee enablement, system integration, and AI cost management, rather than treating each as a separate rollout.

articles.headline: Workday Launches Total Benefits, Bringing Health, Wealth, and Wellbeing Support Together in One Place
articles.blurb: Workday has announced Total Benefits, combining benefits-provider integrations, administration services, and employee guidance in one offering. Workday Wellness is now available to US customers, while benefits guidance through its Self-Service Agent is expected to become generally available in October. Evaluation should cover provider compatibility, sensitive employee-data sharing, and whether the new workflows can replace existing portals and manual administration rather than simply adding another layer.

articles.headline: Anthropic turns Claude into an AI marketplace with 2,000+ plugins and connectors
articles.blurb: Anthropic's marketplace brings together more than 2,000 plugins and connectors, partner-built agents, and services, with eligible partner software purchasable using a portion of committed Anthropic spending. For an internal AI platform team, the significant change is the growing catalog of connections between assistants and business systems, along with another procurement channel to manage. Marketplace availability should not replace reviewing permissions, data access, integration ownership, and how access will be removed when someone leaves.

articles.headline: Microsoft adds pay-as-you-go pricing for extra OneDrive storage
articles.blurb: Microsoft 365 customers can now use consumption-based billing when users exceed their licensed OneDrive storage instead of purchasing additional capacity upfront. Admins choose which users are eligible and can set budgets and alerts. Additional storage costs $0.20/GB/month. Enterprise SaaS is shifting toward usage-based pricing, giving IT more flexibility but also making cost monitoring part of day-to-day platform management.

articles.headline: How to Disable BitLocker in Windows 11 (And When You Shouldn't)
articles.blurb: Disabling BitLocker starts decrypting the drive, while suspending protection leaves the data encrypted but temporarily makes the encryption key accessible. This walkthrough explains the distinction and why short-term firmware maintenance or troubleshooting often calls for suspension rather than removing encryption entirely. The operational takeaway is to make resuming and verifying protection part of the endpoint maintenance runbook, not optional cleanup after the support ticket closes.

articles.headline: New Google Meet 'Take notes for me' settings for admins and end users take effect September 29th
articles.blurb: Google will begin applying new automatic-note settings on September 29.

articles.headline: Cloudflare fixes Containers cross-tenant flaw exposing customer data
articles.blurb: Cloudflare says it completed remediation of a cross-tenant storage-reuse flaw affecting Containers and Sandboxes by September 19, found no evidence of malicious exploitation in available telemetry, and requires no customer-side action.

articles.headline: Dutch Police Arrest ‘Reformed’ Hacker in Shiny Hunters Investigation
articles.blurb: Authorities in the Netherlands have arrested a 23-year-old convicted cybercriminal on suspicion of aiding in data thefts and extortions by the prolific hacker group ShinyHunters. In the days immediately following the suspect's arrest, remaining ShinyHunters members dramatically escalated their attacks, stealing highly sensitive data from the FBI and extorting the Russian ransomware group Cl0p.

articles.headline: U.S. Soldier Gets 70 Months in Prison for AT&T, Verizon Extortions
articles.blurb: A U.S. Army soldier who pleaded guilty to hacking into multiple telecommunications companies and stealing mobile call and text metadata for more than 100 million AT&T customers in 2024 was sentenced to 70 months in federal prison today and ordered to pay nearly $300,000 in restitution to victims.

articles.headline: Data Broker Radaris Loses Domains in Privacy Fight
articles.blurb: The consumer data broker Radaris.com has long had a reputation for ignoring requests to remove personal information from its vast empire of people-search services online. That reputation caught up with the company recently in a lawsuit alleging Radaris violated a New Jersey privacy law that provides for hefty fines against data brokers that publish personal information on state law enforcement officials. In the face of repeated stonewalling and prevarication by attorneys for Radaris, the judge in the case ordered that radaris.com and more than a dozen other data broker domains be transferred to the plaintiffs.

articles.headline: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 1,000 Security Holes
articles.blurb: Microsoft Corp. today issued updates to plug at least 974 security holes in its Windows operating systems and other software, by far its biggest single patch batch ever. Microsoft says artificial intelligence is helping to speed the discovery of vulnerabilities, but security experts warn that many organizations already are struggling to prioritize the more human-intensive endeavor of testing and deploying so many fixes each month.

articles.headline: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses
articles.blurb: A new identity theft service launched on the dark web this week is selling digital scans of more than 153 million drivers licenses from people in the United States and Canada. Based on interviews with individuals whose licenses are available for purchase on this service, it appears to be siphoning images collected by a widely-used identity verification company based in Louisiana. KrebsOnSecurity also has learned that the New Orleans field office of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) today launched an official inquiry into the source of the images.

articles.headline: Two Alleged ‘TeamPCP’ Hackers Arrested in Australia
articles.blurb: Authorities in Australia have arrested two men believed to be members of TeamPCP, a prolific cybercrime and data extortion group blamed for perpetrating the longest running spree of software supply chain attacks ever. In a statement released today, the Australian Federal Police (AFP) said two unnamed suspects from Western Australia, aged 21 and 23, were arrested in connection with a "sophisticated cybercrime syndicate that allegedly created malicious open-source software to rob thousands of global businesses." The AFP did not name the defendants, but KrebsOnSecurity learned the 21-year-old suspect's real identity in June, and has been communicating with him ever since. This story includes interviews with TeamPCP's self-described spokesperson, and examines clues left behind by the TeamPCP leader that likely led to his undoing.

articles.headline: Who’s Tracking You? Use This New Service to Find Out
articles.blurb: It can be daunting to determine who's responsible for showing ads on the websites we visit, or who's harvesting data from the mobile apps we use every day. That information is already semi-public, but it is not easily parsed and traditionally much of it has remained walled away in the hands of large advertising platforms. Not anymore: A powerful and free new service called DecryptAds scrapes and correlates this adtech data and makes it simple to quickly learn a great deal about the entities that are tracking you.

articles.headline: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 400 Security Holes
articles.blurb: Microsoft today released updates to remedy at least 398 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software, including one weakness that is already being actively exploited and two others that were publicly detailed prior to today.

articles.headline: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty in Snowflake Extortions
articles.blurb: A 26-year-old Canadian man once described as one of the most consequential cybercrime threat actors of 2024 has pleaded guilty to computer fraud and conspiracy to hack and extort more than 165 organizations that used the cloud data storage provider Snowflake. Connor Riley Moucka, of Kitchener, Ontario, also admitted to stealing call and text history records of more than 100 million AT&T customers.

articles.headline: Read This Before You Buy That TV Streaming Stick
articles.blurb: Security experts have been sounding the alarm for years about the risks of using generic TV boxes that promise unlimited content streaming for a one-time fee, warning that they secretly rent the user's Internet connection out to strangers. But a groundbreaking new analysis finds these devices also routinely spoof themselves as mobile phones clicking ads on AI-generated websites as part of sprawling operation that seeks to defraud online merchants and advertising networks.

articles.blurb: An attacker used stolen passwords of staff at France's tax administration to take tax data on hundreds of thousands of taxpayers and businesses in June and July. articles.headline: IAM for AI agents: A Practical Enterprise Framework
articles.blurb: What is IAM for AI agents? AI agents authenticate, invoke tools, and act across enterprise systems with delegated authority. The plan has been fiercely criticised by animal rights activists, who say the monkeys should remain roaming freely, and that less destructive options have not been properly considered. Cape Town’s baboon problem has been brewing since the 2000s, after the city stopped culling troops in the late 1990s after pressure from the public.
